t: Maximum Sum of Two Non-Overlapping Subarrays — Prefix Sums and Sliding Bests
o: We must pick two contiguous blocks of fixed lengths `firstLen` (L) and `secondLen` (M) that do not overlap, in either order, maximizing their total sum. In Example 1, the length-2 block [6,5] sums to 11 and the length-1 block [9] sums to 9, giving 20. Example 2 pairs [3,8,1] (12) with [8,9] (17) for 29. Example 3 pairs [5,6,0,9] (20) with [0,3,8] (11) for 31. Since firstLen + secondLen <= n <= 1000, an O(n) or O(n^2) scan is fine; the key is avoiding recomputing subarray sums via prefix sums.
k: Precompute prefix sums so any window sum is O(1).
For each split point, one side's best window can be maintained incrementally as we sweep — this turns brute force into a linear pass.
Handle both orders: L-block before M-block, and M-block before L-block.

a.n: Approach 1: Brute Force over Split Points
a.i: Enumerate every way to place the two windows: for each start of the L-window, try every non-overlapping start of the M-window (both before and after). With prefix sums each candidate pair costs O(1), so total time is O(n^2), which easily fits n <= 1000.
s: Build prefix sums P where P[i] = nums[0..i-1].
For every start i of the L-window (sum = P[i+L]-P[i]), loop starts j < i - M + 1 and j >= i + L for the M-window.
a.t: O(n^2) — for each of ~n positions of the first window we scan all valid positions of the second.

a.i: Sweep the boundary between the two windows. When the L-window ends at index i, the best M-window entirely to its left has some maximum sum we can maintain incrementally; similarly track the best M-window to the right using a precomputed suffix array. Do the same with roles swapped. This gives O(n) time.
s: Build leftMax[k] = max sum of an M-length window ending at or before index k, scanning left to right.
Build rightMax[k] = max sum of an M-length window starting at or after index k, scanning right to left.
For each L-window [i, i+L-1], answer candidate = sL + leftMax[i-1] (M before) and sL + rightMax[i+L] (M after); take the overall max.
a.t: O(n) — three linear passes per ordering, constant number of orderings.
a.sp: O(n) — prefix sums plus the two auxiliary max arrays.

w: In an interview, start with the O(n^2) prefix-sum enumeration to establish correctness, then present the O(n) sliding-maximum solution as the optimization. A common pitfall is forgetting both orderings (M before L and L before M) — running the helper twice with swapped arguments handles it cleanly. Watch off-by-one boundaries: leftMax must cover windows ending strictly before the L-window starts, rightMax windows starting strictly after it ends. Since values are non-negative, initializing `best` to 0 is safe; with negative numbers you would initialize to negative infinity. Follow-ups include generalizing to k non-overlapping windows or handling negative values.
